task_1.title: Recognize GCC 15 in default compiler settings
task_1.description: The update adds GCC major version 15 to the library's default compiler settings so environments using GCC 15 are treated as valid during settings parsing and profile detection. This closes a gap where detected compiler information could reference GCC 15 but the built-in settings model did not include that version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that GCC 15 is accepted as a valid compiler version in the default settings so users working with GCC 15 can use detected or declared compiler settings without version-validation failures.

expectation.grounded: The built-in Conan compiler settings for `compiler=gcc` must include version `15` as a valid public setting value alongside existing GCC versions. Any workflow that consumes the default settings model, including profile detection and settings validation, should accept `compiler.version=15` as a supported GCC value.
expectation.conceptual: Users on GCC 15 should be able to rely on the tool's standard compiler settings and automatic environment detection without the tool rejecting the compiler version as unknown or unsupported.

constraints.grounded: This change must be limited to expanding the accepted GCC version set to include `15`; existing accepted GCC versions and current behavior for other compilers or other GCC subversions must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only remove the compatibility gap for GCC 15 and should not alter how other compiler versions are interpreted or validated.

behavior: The default settings model now recognizes GCC version `15` as a valid `compiler.version` value.
When compiler detection identifies GCC 15, the resulting settings are compatible with the built-in settings schema.
Configurations that explicitly declare GCC 15 no longer fail solely because version `15` was missing from the accepted GCC versions list.
acceptance_criteria: When a user provides settings with `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=15`, the configuration should be accepted by the default settings validation logic.
When a profile or detected environment resolves to GCC 15, it should be usable without requiring a manual settings schema workaround.
When using GCC versions that were already supported before this update, their acceptance and behavior should remain unchanged.
